Small alloy buttons of 30 mm in diameter were prepared by arc melting on a water-cooled copper hearth under an argon gas atmosphere with a non-consumable tungsten electrode. The button ingots were re-melted at least eight times for chemical homogeneity.
The button ingots were then heat treated in a vacuum atmosphere at 1273 K for 0.5 h followed by water quenching in a specially designed heat treatment furnace.

the closed-squares indicate peaks from the α″ phase with orthorhombic crystal structure

The intermediate ω phase is marked by open-diamond. In Ti-24at.%Nb alloy (hereafter denoted as Ti-24Nb alloy) three phase mixtures consisting of α″, ω and β phase are found to display their presence in microstructure.

In Ti-28Nb alloy the diffraction peaks corresponding to β phase are mainly detected to show a matrix phase even though weakly diffracted (110) and (021) peaks of the α″ phase allow their presence within the alloy.

In Ti-28Nb alloy the diffraction peaks corresponding to β phase are mainly detected to show a matrix phase even though weakly diffracted (110) and (021) peaks of the α″ phase allow their presence within the alloy.

In oxygen-added alloys (Ti-24Nb-0.8O and Ti-28Nb-0.8O), a noticeable microstructural change is observed from the analysis of diffraction peaks. The diffraction peaks corresponding to α″ phase is altered to those corresponding to β phase.

In oxygen-added alloys (Ti-24Nb-0.8O and Ti-28Nb-0.8O), a noticeable microstructural change is observed from the analysis of diffraction peaks. The diffraction peaks corresponding to α″ phase is altered to those corresponding to β phase.
Typical martensite structure without showing any other apparent phases is observed as shown in Fig.1 (a).
At the same oxygen content a fully martensite structure was changed to mixed feature consisting of martensite structure and untransformed areas with increasing Nb content
Therefore, it is suggested that oxygen acts to stabilize β phase rather than α stabilizer in quenched state.
Further, Nb addition to Ti gives rise to solid solution hardening.
